5dd2ca5e.text: Shelley's answer is that making something is itself a choice, and a large one. It does not stop being yours the moment you stop looking at it.

9389b9a2.spoken: It watches the De Lacey family work, play music, and go hungry so their blind father can eat.

6f2e4113.spoken: It speaks carefully, in full sentences, and it compares itself to Adam in Paradise Lost.

4b59cac3.text: The creature did not become the opposite of Victor. It became a copy. Here are the two side by side. Victor, the maker, works alone for two years and tells nobody. He abandons what he made. He refuses to admit what he did, even in a courtroom. He chases the creature across Europe to the Arctic and dies still chasing it. Asked to take responsibility, he explains why the situation is not really his fault. The creature, what he made, hides for months and watches through a wall. It is abandoned, then gives up on company entirely. It blames Victor for everything it became. It leads Victor across Europe to the Arctic and never lets him go. Asked to take responsibility, it explains why the situation is not really its fault.

7797be22.text: Norbert Wiener was a mathematician who helped found the study of machines that steer themselves. He saw the problem coming. In 1960 he wrote, in the journal Science: If we use, to achieve our purposes, a mechanical agency with whose operation we cannot efficiently interfere once we have started it, we had better be quite sure that the purpose put into the machine is the purpose which we really desire. Wiener's examples were tales of literal-minded magic, like the monkey's paw, not Frankenstein.
